title: docs(docker): `docker/README.md` pins the runtime image at 14.8.0 — three majors stale against `packages/cli`
body:
Found while implementing #8911 (PR #8960). Out of that card's scope — its file surface was `content/docs/deployment/self-hosting.mdx` only — so filing rather than fixing.

## The defect

`docker/README.md` uses `14.8.0` as its example version in three places:

| Line | Text |
|---|---|
| 32 | `FROM ghcr.io/objectstack-ai/objectstack:14.8.0` |
| 43 | `ghcr.io/objectstack-ai/objectstack:14.8.0` (the `docker run` example) |
| 65 | `docker build -t objectstack:dev --build-arg OS_CLI_VERSION=14.8.0 docker/` |

`packages/cli/package.json` is at **17.0.0**, released to `latest` on 2026-08-14 (`content/docs/releases/v17.mdx`). The examples are three majors behind.

## Why this is a defect and not cosmetic drift

This is not just an out-of-date number. A reader who copies line 32 gets a **v14 runtime**, then builds an artifact with a current v17 CLI — and the runtime refuses that pairing by design: the artifact's `engines.protocol` gate is documented as "Refuses to boot — the safety belt of the two-axis split." So the copy-paste path from this README ends in a boot failure whose cause is one stale digit in the docs.

`self-hosting.mdx` carried the identical staleness in five places; PR #8960 fixed those as part of #8911, because a stale tag sat in what that card promotes to the lead position. `docker/README.md` is the same defect class in a file that card did not own.

## Scope

- Update the three occurrences in `docker/README.md` to the current CLI major.
- Worth deciding at the same time: whether these examples should carry a concrete version at all, or a placeholder. `packages/create-objectstack/src/templates/blank/Dockerfile:26` takes the other approach (`ghcr.io/objectstack-ai/objectstack:latest`), which never goes stale but contradicts the "pin the exact version in production" advice both READMEs give. One convention across the three surfaces would stop this recurring every major.

A concrete-version example goes stale on every major release, so a mechanical guard (a gate asserting docs image tags match `packages/cli`'s major) is the durable fix if this has now happened twice.

Related: #8911, PR #8960.
